_comment: P2P.me — auto Slide-to-Accept. Runs forever: waits for an order popup's 'Slide to Accept' track and performs a trusted drag across it to accept. Nothing else. ALL payment/verification stays manual on your phone. The platform CHANGED (verified live 2026-08-05): acceptance is now a SLIDE, not a Close-then-Accept click. Clicking 'Close' now REJECTS the order — this recipe never does that. See _flow, _safety and _targeting_notes before changing anything.
_how_to_run:
truklick run recipes/p2p-me/recipe.json      (opens its own browser; log in once, it keeps you logged in)
Stop with Ctrl+C, or press the hotkey below to pause/resume if your OS grants it.
See docs/QUICKSTART.md.
_flow: Order popup appears with a 'Slide to Accept' slider (accept) and a 'Close' LINK (reject). Slide to Accept -> a payment popup with a 'Slide to Complete' slider appears (WON). 'Slide to Complete' MOVES REAL MONEY and is done by hand on the phone; this recipe never touches it. If another merchant accepts first, a 'not accepted by you' dialog with a real Close BUTTON appears (LOST) — step 1 clears that at the top of the next pass.
_safety:
Exact-string matching is the safety boundary. The swipe targets text EXACTLY equal to 'Slide to Accept', so it can NEVER match 'Slide to Complete' (the money step) — a different string. There is no Close-to-reject step. The only Close this recipe ever clicks is role=button (the LOST-dialog dismissal); the order popup's reject-Close is a

and never matches role=button. If any target fails to resolve we WAIT rather than act — on a payments dashboard, not acting is the safe failure.
_targeting_notes:
DO NOT replace these with CSS selectors. lp.p2p.me is React; the popup is a Radix dialog whose container id is generated per render, so CSS paths break on every popup. The slider renders as nested elements that all report the SAME box except a narrow inner label: 'Slide to Accept' also appears on a ~105px

INSIDE the ~400px track. min_width:300 keeps only the wide track, so the drag spans the whole slider and not its label. Read the track's live box each run (its y varies with popup placement) — never hardcode coordinates.
_reliability: P2P.me offers the same order to several merchants; first to complete the slide wins, so some cycles legitimately end with the order gone. That is competition, not a fault. The expect step distinguishes them: EXPECT OK = payment screen ('Slide to Complete') appeared = we got it; EXPECT FAILED = someone else did (or it expired). The run summary reports the success rate. Field note: the slider stays up ~1-2 min, so this is not a pure millisecond race — a browser drag (~200ms, animation-gated) can still lose to a merchant calling the accept API directly.
name: P2P.me — auto slide-to-accept

steps._note: Clears a leftover 'not accepted by you' dialog from a previous lost order so the loop stays clean. This Close is a real

Waits for the next order popup's slide track. min_width:300 selects the wide track, not the ~105px inner label. Times out after 120s only to re-arm the loop (and clear any LOST dialog) — it keeps waiting for orders forever.

Trusted drag across the whole track: grab ~24px in (the knob sits just inside the left), move in 30 steps @6ms, hold 120ms at the end, release. The slider watches for realistic motion; an instant jump or a release-on-arrival does not register. Delete THIS step to make the recipe watch-only (never accept).

steps.name: order accepted (payment screen 'Slide to Complete' shown)
steps._note: Verifies the OUTCOME, not just that we dragged. The payment popup's 'Slide to Complete' appears only if WE won the order. Absent = another merchant took it (or it expired). We only DETECT this string — never act on it.

_speed: poll_ms is deliberately modest (30ms wait, 50ms expect). The slider stays up ~1-2 min (see _reliability), so shaving poll further does not win more orders and just burns CPU. Raise the pads/steps/hold to tune the drag feel; lower poll_ms only if you have measured it helps.
